claims.text: Annealing that enhances chemical short-range order increases yield strength relative to rapid quenching.
The strength increase caused by enhanced short-range order arises from localized lattice distortions that pin dislocations.
Al0.1CrCoFeNi can have a single-phase A1 structure.
The proposed homogenized initial alloy is chemically disordered and has minimal inherent short-range order.
Rapid quenching can freeze a comparatively random atomic arrangement with minimal short-range order.
A targeted annealing treatment can increase chemical short-range order without changing overall composition or phase.
The comparison holds composition, global phase, and loading conditions constant while varying short-range order.
Chemical short-range order manifests as localized lattice distortions and heterogeneous local stress fields.
Short-range-order-induced local stress fields act as pinning points for dislocations.
Dislocation pinning by short-range order modifies deformation or failure behavior relative to a random atomic distribution.
Enhanced-short-range-order samples will have higher yield strength than rapidly quenched samples under identical loading conditions.
Enhanced-short-range-order samples will show a different dislocation density, dislocation distribution, or failure mode.
The proposed relationship should hold in single-phase disordered multi-component alloys under quasi-static loading from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures.
The hypothesis excludes alloys that undergo phase separation or compositional changes during processing.
Al content influences lattice ordering and phase stability in AlxCrCoFeNi.
TEM can be used to compare dislocation density and configurations between the treated states.
Atom-probe tomography or diffraction can be used to assess local chemical order.
Failure to observe a statistically significant strength increase or a distinct dislocation response despite confirmed enhanced short-range order would falsify the proposed strengthening mechanism.
